cells.tense: You are standing at the end of a long stretch of holding many true things at once, and it is working.
cells.ask: Pick the one thing you started that is already finished, say out loud that it is done, and set it down.
cells.core:
You're holding a lot of true things at once right now, and it isn't cluttering you. You can tell which perceptions have run their course and which are still forming, and you say so plainly enough that people around you feel steadier. Nothing here needs fixing.

Keeping it takes something, though. Knowing which of many true things is done is a decision you make again and again, and it stays clean only if you keep making it. Name the thing that's complete, hand it over as complete, and let whatever is next arrive on its own schedule. The same clarity that reaches people is the clarity you keep giving yourself.
cells.sheetLine: You can tell what's finished, and you say so cleanly.
cells.verb: holding many true things at once and telling which have finished
cells.place: the point of departure that is also arrival

cells.tense: You are bracing toward a finish you are trying to force before its time.
cells.ask: Pick one unfinished thing and leave it alone for a day, saying nothing about it to anyone, so it can finish on its own.
cells.core:
You've got a picture of how this all wraps up, and you're rushing toward it. Whole conclusions get spoken before the pieces have gathered. People feel the push more than the perception, and the part that used to land cleanly has started sliding past them.

What you're after is real, and it will not arrive on command. The choice that matters is smaller than the finish line: pick one direction for the next stretch and let everything else sit unwritten. Then say what you actually notice instead of what you've decided the whole thing means. Your read of it sharpens when you give it room to complete.

cells.tense: Something that already finished is still sitting in your hands, and you have not put it down.
cells.ask: Find one thing you could hand to the right person today, tell them what you notice in it, and pass it over.
cells.core:
You notice more than you're letting on, and you're not spending it. The reading is running — you see what's in front of you and what's between people — but it stays inside, and it has been staying inside for a while. Silence has gotten comfortable, and the longer it holds, the easier it is to keep holding.

What's absent isn't insight. It's the step where what you see meets someone else's view and the two of you make something neither of you could alone. Find one thing you know that belongs with another person right now, and put it in front of them. Not a performance. Just the honest read, said plain.
cells.sheetLine: You know what you see, and you're keeping it to yourself.

cells.tense: You are deciding what is fair and complete in this stretch without saying that you are the one deciding.
cells.ask: Say out loud to one person that a call you made about what was fair or finished was yours.
cells.core:
You're already weighing what's fair and what's done in this stretch — which thing is owed, which thing is over, who gets what. It shapes what you say and what you let go, and it's steady enough that people feel it. That steadiness is real, and it's doing work in the room.

And you describe it as though the situation were deciding by itself. This judgment is yours; you're the one doing it, and it's a private read that hasn't been said in your own voice yet. Hand one call over as yours, to the person who needs to hear it. It gets lighter, not heavier, and what's already working gets to work out loud.
cells.sheetLine: You're already deciding what's fair. Say that it's your call.
